findings.title: IdP queries were blocked by 403
findings.evidence: entitlements/github_members_vs_idp and entitlements/idp_groups both returned HTTP 403 from Entra ID; IdP data was unreachable for this tenant
findings.proposed_remediation: Grant the StackQL app registration Microsoft Graph consent or otherwise restore Entra ID query access, then rerun the entitlements checks

findings.summary: The AWS account has four IAM users with AdministratorAccess. Two appear to be non-human or demo admin principals and two appear to be human users. GitHub outside-collaborator admin checks returned no findings, and Entra ID queries were blocked with HTTP 403, so IdP-based orphan/leaver checks could not be completed.

assessments.rationale: The IAM user `oape-demo-admin-user` has direct attachment of AWS managed `AdministratorAccess`, which is account-wide privilege in AWS account 824532806693. The `oape-demo` prefix suggests a demo principal, but demo status does not justify unrestricted administrative access; correlation with three other AdministratorAccess users indicates broader entitlement sprawl. IdP access was blocked, so human ownership confirmation is required before recertification can be considered complete.
assessments.remediation_plan: 1. Have the AWS account owner and the oape-demo demo owner confirm whether `oape-demo-admin-user` is still required. 2. Replace `AdministratorAccess` with least privilege: a customer-managed policy limited to required demo actions and, where supported, resources tagged `purpose=oape-demo` or named with prefix `oape-demo`; prefer short-lived role assumption over a standing IAM user. 3. Validate no critical demo workflow depends on account-wide admin. 4. Detach `AdministratorAccess` from the user using the StackQL DELETE below. 5. Rerun the entitlement check and restore Entra ID/IdP query access so ownership can be independently reconciled.
assessments.remediation_sql:
DELETE FROM aws.iam.attached_user_policies
WHERE user_name = 'oape-demo-admin-user'
  AND policy_arn = 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess'
  AND region = 'us-east-1';
assessments.blast_radius: Removes only the direct `AdministratorAccess` managed-policy attachment from IAM user `oape-demo-admin-user`; it does not delete the user, access keys, inline policies, group-derived permissions, or other users. Demo automation using this user may fail if it relies on unrestricted AWS administration.

assessments.rationale: The IAM user `stackql` has direct `AdministratorAccess`, giving any holder of its credentials full control of AWS account 824532806693. Because this appears to be an automation/tooling principal, standing account-admin privilege is especially risky and should be replaced with narrowly scoped audit/remediation permissions. The other AdministratorAccess findings and blocked IdP data increase concern that ownership and necessity have not been recently recertified.
assessments.remediation_plan: 1. Have the platform engineering owner for StackQL automation and the AWS account owner confirm whether the `stackql` IAM user is still required. 2. Replace `AdministratorAccess` with least privilege: preferably an assumable role with short-lived credentials and only the read-only inventory permissions plus specific remediation actions StackQL actually performs in this tenancy. 3. Confirm StackQL workflows still run under the reduced policy in AWS account 824532806693. 4. Detach `AdministratorAccess` from the user using the StackQL DELETE below. 5. Rerun the entitlement sweep and resolve the Entra ID 403 so the principal can be reconciled against authoritative ownership records.
assessments.remediation_sql:
DELETE FROM aws.iam.attached_user_policies
WHERE user_name = 'stackql'
  AND policy_arn = 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess'
  AND region = 'us-east-1';
assessments.blast_radius: Removes only the direct `AdministratorAccess` managed-policy attachment from IAM user `stackql`; it does not delete the user, keys, inline policies, group-derived permissions, or other principals. StackQL automation may lose the ability to perform unrestricted mutations and should be tested against the intended least-privilege policy.

executive_summary: Both escalated findings are material: two AWS IAM users in account 824532806693 have direct `AdministratorAccess`, and the broader sweep shows two additional admin users plus blocked IdP access, indicating entitlement sprawl and incomplete ownership verification. Recertify each principal with the named service/demo or platform owner, replace standing admin with narrowly scoped policies or short-lived roles, detach the AWS managed admin policy, then rerun the entitlement checks after restoring IdP query access.
